title: Impact of strain relaxation on performance of α-formamidinium lead iodide perovskite solar cells
finding: Relaxing residual strain in α-FAPbI₃ suppresses the transition to the photoinactive δ-phase, stabilizing the black perovskite and boosting device performance.

title: Strain engineering in perovskite solar cells and its impacts on carrier dynamics
finding: Depth-dependent GIXRD reveals a gradient of in-plane residual strain; strain-induced band bending (DFT) governs carrier dynamics, and controlled strain modulation yields 20.7% certified PCE.

title: Strained hybrid perovskite thin films and their impact on the intrinsic stability of perovskite solar cells
finding: Landmark demonstration that MAPbI₃ films are residually strained relative to substrates from thermal-expansion mismatch during annealing, degrading intrinsic stability.

title: Band Gap Tuning via Lattice Contraction and Octahedral Tilting in Perovskite Materials for Photovoltaics
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
finding: Lattice contraction and octahedral tilting (via A/B-cation size) tune bandgap and phase behaviour, establishing the composition→lattice→property link underpinning strain design.

title: Light-induced lattice expansion leads to high-efficiency perovskite solar cells
finding: Light-soaking drives a reversible ~0.1–0.3% lattice expansion that relaxes local strain at grain boundaries/interfaces, uniformly raising efficiency across architectures.

title: Strain engineering and epitaxial stabilization of halide perovskites
finding: Epitaxial growth on lattice-mismatched single-crystal substrates imposes controllable compressive/tensile strain and stabilizes otherwise-metastable halide-perovskite phases.

title: Regulating strain in perovskite thin films through charge-transport layers
finding: Compressive strain injected from a high-thermal-expansion HTL compensates residual tensile strain, raising the ion-migration activation energy; 16.4% wide-bandgap cell keeps 96% after 85 °C/1000 h.

title: Strain analysis and engineering in halide perovskite photovoltaics
finding: Reference review defining strain analysis (GIWAXS, XRD sin²ψ, Williamson–Hall) and engineering routes; frames residual strain as an intrinsic, encapsulation-immune instability channel.

title: Lattice strain causes non-radiative losses in halide perovskites
finding: Spatially-resolved strain patterns across films correlate with shortened carrier lifetimes, directly tying local lattice strain to non-radiative recombination losses.

title: Interfacial Residual Stress Relaxation in Perovskite Solar Cells with Improved Stability
finding: Interfacial residual tensile stress relaxed by a strain-releasing interlayer, improving both efficiency and operational/thermal stability of the device stack.

title: Synergistic strain engineering of perovskite single crystals for highly stable and sensitive X-ray detectors with low-bias imaging and monitoring
finding: Synergistic strain engineering in perovskite single crystals reduces defect density and enhances stability, extending strain control beyond polycrystalline films.

title: Strain effects on halide perovskite solar cells
finding: Comprehensive review linking tensile/compressive strain to ion migration, defect formation, halide segregation and phase stability across the strain-effect landscape.

title: Strain in perovskite solar cells: origins, impacts and regulation
finding: Review establishing that residual tensile strain — unlike moisture/heat — cannot be countered by encapsulation, and surveys origins, characterization and regulation.

title: Elimination of Interfacial Lattice Mismatch and Detrimental Reaction by Self‐Assembled Layer Dual‐Passivation for Efficient and Stable Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
finding: Eliminating interfacial lattice mismatch removes a strain source and a detrimental interfacial reaction, improving stability of the perovskite/charge-transport junction.

title: Revealing the strain-associated physical mechanisms impacting the performance and stability of perovskite solar cells
finding: Resolves the microscopic mechanisms by which residual strain degrades performance, connecting lattice distortion to defect populations and transport.

title: Revealing Steric‐Hindrance‐Dependent Buried Interface Defect Passivation Mechanism in Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells with Mitigated Tensile Stress
finding: Steric-hindrance-tuned molecular passivation at the buried interface simultaneously relieves interfacial lattice strain and passivates defects.

title: Lattice Compression Increases the Activation Barrier for Phase Segregation in Mixed-Halide Perovskites
finding: Hydrostatic lattice compression raises the activation barrier for photoinduced halide segregation in mixed-halide films — direct evidence that compressive strain suppresses phase separation.

title: Strain regulation retards natural operation decay of perovskite solar cells
finding: Under day/night cycling, periodic thermal strain (absent in continuous-mode tests) drives trap accumulation and chemical decay; phenylselenenyl chloride regulates strain for 26.3% certified PCE and 10× T80 improvement.

title: Strain Engineering in Halide Perovskites
finding: Early framing review cataloguing strain sources (thermal-mismatch, lattice-mismatch, composition) and their coupling to optoelectronic and stability properties.

title: Strain Modulation for Light‐Stable n–i–p Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
finding: Strain modulation produces light-stable n–i–p perovskite/silicon tandem sub-cells, mitigating photoinduced strain-driven degradation in wide-bandgap tops.

title: Strain Control to Stabilize Perovskite Solar Cells
finding: Demonstrates strain control as a general handle to stabilize perovskite solar cells against operational stressors.

title: The influence of strain on phase stability in mixed-halide perovskites
finding: Systematic study showing applied strain shifts the thermodynamics/kinetics of halide phase separation in mixed-halide perovskites, coupling strain state to compositional stability.

title: Taming Lattice Strain via Buried Interface Engineering for Reverse-Bias Resilient Perovskite Solar Cells
finding: Identifies the buried HTL/perovskite interface as the principal strain-accumulation site; a fluorinated anchor (3F-2TC) relieves strain (GIWAXS-confirmed), giving 26.10% PCE and 91.58% retention after 200 h at −1.0 V reverse bias.
